pr_title: host/l2cap: fix sending error codes in connection requests
pr_body:
Fixes issues related to Enhanced Credit Based connection request.

Fixes: #35840
pr_comments:
Could you update the commit message to use ":" instead of "/"
And preferable start with Bluetooth, so "Bluetooth: host: "
Removed unnecessary error translation - it was already done in `l2cap_chan_accept()`
@carlescufi Rebased, but I'll return to this PR because it's not finished

@joerchan I updated the PR, now first commit has appropriate message (it fixes missing 0x0000 CIDs). I fixed the code accoriding to your revew. As of L2CAP/ECFC/BV-27-C, there is TSE15410, which confirms that MTU larger than something is nonsense, and it should be smaller. I think we should introduce some config setting for L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MTU - it could be 64 for by default, could be set to any larger value. If MTU in req is smaller than 64 we shall return BT_L2CAP_LE_ERR_INVALID_PARAMS, and if smaller than L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MTU - BT_L2CAP_LE_ERR_UNACCEPT_PARAMS. According to TSE, we will need L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MTU larger than 64.
For L2CAP/ECFC/BV-26-C I submitted support request CASE0071314 (PTS doesn't see response)
Please link this to an issue that it fixes if this should be merged for 2.6. AFAIK only PRs that close issues are accepted at this late stage of the release process.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: host: L2CAP enhanced connection request conformance test issues
issue_context.body:
During PTS (Bluetooth host confurmance) testing some issues have been discovered with the Enhanced Credit Based connection request.

 - Missing 0x0000 CIDs in the connection response when all connections have been refused.

 - Wrong error code returned in certain cases.
   - Expected "some connections refused - reason" but received "success".
   - Expected "invalid parameters" but "unacceptable parameters" was received.
 
The following test cases are affected:
 - L2CAP/ECFC/BV-20-C
 - L2CAP/ECFC/BV-26-C

review_comments: The declaration of rc can be moved into this while loop.

Since there is no else to this, it means that if none of the above happens we would use buf, which is pointing to the original request to send the response. That wouldn't be a good idea I think. Is there any way we could end up in a hypothetical else here?
Commit message doesn't match what the code is doing, should be updated to say "the last one that failed" (or something similar).

The le_conn_req is ignoring the packet, while le_ecred_conn_req is responding with invalid parameters. @Vudentz is that correct for le_conn_req? I find it strange that they would behave so differently for this.

I don't see tests for this MTU check for L2CAP without ECFC. Also, Core specification doesn't tell anything about these errors, only lists their codes. Maybe this can be added to `le_conn_req` too, but it shouldn't affect any tests.

I was referring to this: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/715b68d389b9cdb75208a48663035c48a34828b0/subsys/bluetooth/host/l2cap.c#L1044L1047

It is not related to your changes here, I just find it weird.

Do you know if there is any tests that verifies that behavior?
Yes, that’s what I meant. I haven’t seen any tests of this, for not enhanced credit flow control
